chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Leaving Homestead and how the town has changed
summary: Few people she knew are left; she turned professional in 1936.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When I left Homestead to come to New York, I had been working at this club in Pittsburgh and I didn't get back to Homestead for two years. And when I would go back to Homestead, I would go back working in the theater or something like that, so I really didn't get a chance to get around to see everybody that I had known. And now, I don't suppose
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
there are that many people around that I knew when I was younger.
You may be surprised when you go back in August.

No, I've been back since and it's sort of sad, you know, there just aren't that many people around that I knew as a youngster. Even when I was in Homestead before I came to New York when I worked in the club, I didn't get out very much. I worked downtown in Pittsburgh so when I'd come home I'd go to bed. So for several years, even before I tried to come to New York, I was practically out of touch. I worked late hours and I had to sleep, and by the time I'd get up and eat and get ready to go to work, it would be, you know, -- I'd be away because the hours that I worked would be quite late. I worked in an after-hours spot and I'd get home 6 or 7 o'clock in the morning and I'd sleep practically all day.
So I was practically out of touch with what was going on locally, really.
In the early days, long before I

considered myself as having become professional, which was 1936, that one job that I had -- I sang around little clubs around Homestead. I wasn't making a living at it, but if there was anything going on like a dance or like a club had a group there, I would show up and sing. I guess I got my early experience that way.
